los.text: Locate the pituitary gland (hypophysis cerebri) within the sella turcica of the sphenoid bone
los.html:
Pituitary (hypophysis cerebri)Sits in the sella turcica (hypophyseal fossa) on the body of the sphenoid bone.
StalkThe infundibulum joins it to the hypothalamus, passing through the diaphragma sellae.
SurgeryReached transsphenoidally (through the nose and sphenoid sinus).

los.text: Label a diagram of the parts of the pituitary gland, namely the anterior lobe (adenohypophysis), pars anterior (pars distalis), pars intermedia, pars tuberalis and posterior lobe (neurohypophysis)
los.html:
LobePartsProducts
Anterior (adenohypophysis)Pars distalis (pars anterior): the bulkGH, prolactin, ACTH, TSH, FSH, LH
Pars intermedia: thin band next to the posterior lobeMSH (rudimentary in humans)
Pars tuberalis: wraps round the stalkFew hormones
Posterior (neurohypophysis)Pars nervosa, infundibular stalk, median eminenceStores and releases ADH and oxytocin, made in the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei
Hypophyseal portal system
  • Hypothalamic releasing hormones go via the median eminence and portal veins to the anterior lobe
  • The posterior lobe gets axons directly.
Stalk compressionDopamine can't reach the anterior lobe, so prolactin rises (stalk effect).

los.text: Describe the anatomical relationships of the pituitary gland (diaphragma sellae, sphenoid, cavernous sinus, dorsum sellae, basilar artery, the pons)
los.html:
DirectionRelationClinical
AboveDiaphragma sellae, then the optic chiasm, hypothalamus, 3rd ventricleMacroadenoma → bitemporal hemianopia
BelowSphenoid body and sphenoid sinusTranssphenoidal approach
Each sideCavernous sinus: ICA, CN VI (free in the sinus), III, IV, V1, V2 in the wallLateral spread → ophthalmoplegia (VI often first)
BehindDorsum sellae, then the basilar artery and pons
In frontTuberculum sellae, anterior clinoid processes

los.text: Identify the thyroid and parathyroid glands, noting the arterial supply and venous drainage of each and the relationship of the arteries with the laryngeal nerves and the strap muscles
los.html:
• Thyroid: two lobes joined by the isthmus over tracheal rings 2–4
    • inside the pretracheal fascia, so it moves up on swallowing
    • ± pyramidal lobe.
VesselOrigin / drainageNerve relation
Superior thyroid arteryFirst branch of the ECAExternal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve runs close: tie the artery close to the gland (voice pitch, cricothyroid)
Inferior thyroid arteryThyrocervical trunk (subclavian)Recurrent laryngeal nerve crosses near it: tie the artery away from the gland
Thyroid ima arteryBrachiocephalic trunk or arch (~10%)Bleeding risk at tracheostomy
Superior and middle thyroid veins→ IJV
Inferior thyroid veins→ brachiocephalic veins
Strap (infrahyoid) musclesSternohyoid, sternothyroid, omohyoid, thyrohyoid lie in front; ansa cervicalis (C1–3) enters them low, so cut them high.
ParathyroidsUsually 4, on the back of the thyroid lobes; blood mainly from the inferior thyroid artery.
ParathyroidOriginPosition
Superior4th pouchMore constant; near the cricothyroid joint and RLN entry
Inferior3rd pouch (with the thymus)Variable: can lie low in the neck or in the mediastinum
  • RLN damage: hoarse voice (one side); stridor and airway obstruction (both).

los.text: Identify the processes by which the pituitary gland, thyroid gland and suprarenal glands develop and name the parts of these developing embryonic structures
los.html:
GlandPartEmbryonic originRemnants / problems
PituitaryAnteriorRathke's pouch: ectoderm from the roof of the primitive mouth (stomodeum)Craniopharyngioma
PosteriorInfundibulum: neuroectoderm growing down from the diencephalon
ThyroidFollicular cells
  • Endoderm at the foramen caecum of the tongue
  • Descends in front of the hyoid via the thyroglossal duct (to its final place by week 7)
Thyroglossal cyst (midline, moves up when the tongue is stuck out), lingual thyroid, pyramidal lobe
C (parafollicular) cellsUltimobranchial body (4th pouch), neural crestMedullary thyroid cancer (calcitonin)
ParathyroidsInferior / superior3rd / 4th pharyngeal pouchesEctopic glands; DiGeorge (3rd and 4th pouches fail)
SuprarenalCortexMesoderm (coelomic epithelium of the posterior abdominal wall)Large fetal cortex shrinks after birth; congenital adrenal hyperplasia
MedullaNeural crest (chromaffin cells = modified sympathetic neurons)Phaeochromocytoma, neuroblastoma

los.text: Locate the pineal gland and describe its function
los.html:
Pineal glandSmall midline body on the roof of the 3rd ventricle, above the superior colliculi.
Function
  • Secretes melatonin in the dark, setting circadian rhythm.
  • Pathway: retina → suprachiasmatic nucleus → sympathetic chain (superior cervical ganglion) → pineal.
Calcifies with age("brain sand")a useful midline marker on CT and X-ray.
Pineal tumoursPress on the tectum (Parinaud's syndrome: can't look up) and block the aqueduct (obstructive hydrocephalus).
